mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2% over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with reduced consumer demand, which negatively impacts corporate earnings and drives lower S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months signals weakening labor market conditions, which depresses wage growth and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and a decline in consumer sentiment (proxied by RSAFS) above their respective 3-month moving averages signals a restrictive monetary policy environment with weakening demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: restrictive monetary policy with falling consumer sentiment
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the housing starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both the unemployment rate and payroll employment (PAYEMS) month-over-month, where unemployment rises but payroll employment also rises, indicates labor market churning; this ambiguity signals uncertainty and leads to lower S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases AND PAYEMS increases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annual increase in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above 3% for six consecutive quarters signals a robust demand environment that supports corporate earnings growth and results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 70% of quarters where GDPC1 grows above 3% for six consecutive quarters.
